7,276 bytes and four dispatch tables: `inPhase3` picks the phase, and
`word_3c` -- which the member copies out of `equalizer->stateCount` on
entry -- picks the state within it.
26 CAUGHT AND 74 NOT CAUGHT, AND THE 74 ARE KEPT ON PURPOSE.  They are not
unusable and they are not equivalent: each compiles, each runs, and each
produced a real verdict against a GREEN baseline.  What they say is that
this fixture cannot present the `word_3c` arms, and 7484's rule is that
'we tried this and it survived for a reason' beats an absent entry, which
reads as nobody having thought of it.  Deleting them would leave a suite
reading 26 of 26 -- a headline that looks perfect because its denominator
was removed, which is the one shape CLAUDE.md spends four paragraphs on.
Finding F6000 does NOT license the deletion: that rule is about a DECLARED
binary, which cannot score a suite at all; this baseline exits zero.
WHY THE ARMS CANNOT BE PRESENTED, and it is the equaliser rather than the
source.  `V90Equalizer::process` runs between any poke and `progress`'s
read: it sets `stateCount = 0` on entry and refills it from
`phase3Demod->word_30` or `phase4Demod->int_0028`, both of which its own
`getDecision` call has already rewritten.  The sweep therefore takes
whichever arm the receive chain produced -- three distinct ones of the
thirty-one the two tables dispatch -- identically on both sides.  Driving
the rest means walking the equaliser to each of its events, which is
`t_v90equproc`'s object.  Finding F7513, which also records what happened
when the equaliser WAS wired deep enough to take its PHASE3 arm.
WHAT IS PROSE IN FINDING F7512 RATHER THAN A MUTATION HERE:
* the `(int)inPhase3 > 2` cast in the remote-retrain arm.  The object
compares with a SIGNED `jg` on a field the header declares
`unsigned int`; over the 0, 1, 2, 3 and 5 the class can reach the two
readings agree for every value, so codegen is the only evidence and
no differential test can fail on it.  613's shape.
* the two `phase3Demodulator->byte_3f8 = 0x74;` stores.  They may be two
different named constants in the original that happen to be equal;
nothing in the object separates them.
